text: ChallengeLens. Check proposal timing before the bond.

ChallengeLens checks proposal timing before an operator posts a bond. Of five hundred ninety-eight sampled disputed UMA requests, two hundred sixty-six settled too early. This is a selected sample, not the rate across all proposals. SERV reads the governing clause, code checks the cutoff, and event evidence checks what happened before the proposal.

The desk screens proposals in their challenge windows about every three minutes. This snapshot has {{in_liveness}} proposals and {{bond_usdc}} USDC in bonds; some already confirmed on time by the sports feed, some read by SERV, and {{flagged}}. Many have no deterministic key yet. Missing keys remain unresolved. A feed screen and a SERV reading are separate; zero flags does not prove there are no premature proposals.

Paste a market, choose a side and check now. Here we choose the first Bitcoin example, a market, and Yes. Check timing. SERV quotes the rule and copies its local clock; code converts it to UTC. Code checks the cutoff, and required event evidence must agree. The action says Proceed, Wait, or what evidence is still needed.

This Braves proposal came before the feed's final mark. Moving past it changes only the local preview. Now I request a fresh SERV reading at this proposal time. With SERV and the completion evidence agreeing, the action becomes Proceed. The receipt records the inputs and hashes.

On sixty new cases, SERV alone approved nineteen of twenty-eight too-early proposals. With checks: zero of twenty-eight, with a Wilson ninety-five percent upper bound of twelve point one percent. Checks alone also had zero. Deterministic checks produced this result; SERV did not improve accuracy. Proceed coverage was forty-four percent: fourteen of thirty-two timing-OK cases. Repeats are not independent samples.

Proceed checks timing, not whether the proposed outcome is correct. UMA settlements are proxy labels. Sports feeds lag, and missing evidence holds a check. The desk never recommends disputing. This is not financial advice.

Reppo reviews saved verdicts. A block, rejection, or routed review scoring below seventy can hold Proceed; it never upgrades an action. A real Proceed scored fifty-two and was held. We added missing context; the same case scored sixty-nine, still held. One review each, so this shows the loop works, not that accuracy improved.
